legacy_contract.indices: 1-based decimal string fields; actual File/Blob chunk can have empty, application/octet-stream or video/mp4 MIME
legacy_contract.no_full_file_attestation: Old protocol supplies neither total_size nor a complete SHA256 manifest. MD5 is an opaque client identity, not a claimed original-byte digest. Server calculates and fixes the SHA256/size of each first accepted part.
legacy_contract.md5_provenance: Actual old client uses FileReader.readAsBinaryString(file), then js-md5(binaryString).
legacy_contract.identity: APP_KEY HMAC(domain, supplier_id, actor_id, filename, normalized client_md5) yields the same UUIDv4-shaped legacy session on retries. Session initialization additionally fixes all manifest fields; changed category/count/chunk size is rejected.

pid_undefined.actual_trigger: productDetails.videoSaveToUrl and productEdit.videoSaveToUrl omit pid; FormData.append sends literal undefined.
pid_undefined.php: (int) pid resolves this to root category0.
pid_undefined.ts: Only legacy adapter accepts exact null or string undefined as0; modern pid remains bounded integer.

final.att_id: same actual attachment ID across final replays
final.name: canonical /api/assets/<id>

responses.replay: Committed nonfinal-part replay still returns code1; final-part replay returns code2 and the same attachment identity. This preserves the actual old sequential Promise consumer.

external_registration.response: Supplier metadata DTO {att_id,name,url,src,cover_image,type}; existing TS Supplier shape retained. PHP true is provenance, not claimed byte-identical response.
external_registration.limits: Normalized HTTPS MP4 URL/controlled optional image cover each <=200 characters; deterministic name <100; real_name <=255; no remote HEAD/download/cover generation; upload_type cannot select a cloud driver.

modern_contract.upload_id: Client lowercase UUIDv4 is persisted before any mutation; recovery queries the original UUID.
modern_contract.content_checks: Server validates MP4 ftyp content, exact declared part size/SHA, immutable first part bytes and ordered re-read digests before composing; client hashing reads one bounded slice at a time.
modern_contract.progress: Only durable server-confirmed part numbers contribute upload progress.
modern_contract.unknown_result: No timeout/failure is a successful save. Query the original UUID; a committed receipt returns the original attachment and never allocates another upload. Immutable active parts can be resent to repair missing/corrupt R2 bytes; explicit force repair retransmits all originals.
modern_contract.cancellation: Abort current request first, write the same UUID immutable tombstone, query if its result is unknown; terminal rows cannot reopen or be deleted/truncated.

authority.tenant: Supplier ID comes from signed Supplier JWT actor -> current active system_admin.relation_id -> active system_supplier, never body/query/header tenant fields.
authority.actor: Every existing upload row binds both actor_id and supplier_id; HMAC domain, immutable root identity and storage paths bind the same tuple.
authority.live_checks: Every reservation/publication transaction holds actual authority table barriers and checks password auth-version, DB wall-clock JWT expiry, active account/tenant and current role/menu permission before and after work. Repeated after provider I/O and before attachment publication.

permissions.query_cancel: authenticated active original actor+supplier; manage withdrawal alone does not block recovery/cancellation

authority.category: Video category must be exact type4/relation=current supplier/file_type2 under actual category+attachment fence; root0 allowed.
authority.frontend_identity: supplier-token, supplier-user(id,supplier_id), supplier-permissions and actual supplier-session-changed/storage events; token/permission/tenant/actor/context epochs abort old requests and reject late replies including A->B->A.

session_storage.failure: Read/parse/write failure gates all mutations until explicit successful recovery read.

product_reference_contract.stable: Uploaded private video is saved only as canonical /api/assets/<id> in video_link; video_open derives from nonempty saved reference.
product_reference_contract.display: video_preview_url is a separate read projection. Temporary preview tickets are rendered only, stripped from editable form/save bodies, and never replace stable references.
product_reference_contract.explicit_use: Upload completion creates a library asset only. The user must click 使用此视频 to update the current product draft, then separately save the product.
product_reference_contract.private_policy: Canonical refs always verify actual product-video module1/file2/image8/MP4 MIME/key and ownership within the save transaction under the real attachment fence, even when unchanged. Platform video may be shared; Supplier private video is same active supplier only.

legacy_compatibility_exception.condition: Existing product belongs to the current Supplier; input normalized value exactly equals its current stored legacy videoLink; value is noncanonical.
legacy_compatibility_exception.behavior: Unchanged legacy public value may be retained while editing other fields. New or changed refs and every canonical private ref still assert policy. Read retains the editable value, but invalid old values receive empty preview and no private signature.
legacy_compatibility_exception.risk: Intentional low-risk compatibility exception retains historical external-value risk; this is not data cleansing or a grant of private asset authority. Public consumers retain existing historical rendering semantics.
legacy_compatibility_exception.http_regression: supplier-product-media.test.ts keeps HTTP legacy read and unchanged save, rejects changed HTTP and foreign/malformed private refs, and asserts no provider access.

standalone_addon.install: Explicit PG16 owner-maintenance transaction only; never HTTP, historical bootstrap, runAll, root SQL or ORM. Install/grant SELECT INSERT UPDATE to a separate restricted runtime identity before enabling the routes.
standalone_addon.catalog_guard: Exact13 columns/5CHECKs/7constraints/2indexes/2triggers/function body+owner+ACL+runtime privilege proof; partial/drifted addons fail closed without repair.
standalone_addon.facts_guard: Header tuple immutable; only OLD active -> active/cancelled/committed; updated_at monotone; parts/confirmed monotone; terminal rows reject update/delete/truncate. Parts object <=100 and <=16KiB; confirmed array <=100; detailed structure and HMAC rechecked in service.
standalone_addon.declaration_audit: Only independent current-product declaration scope adds source full SHA +13columns. Fixed current worker declarations306->307, product addons2->3; historical/current-ordinary cohorts and hashes, runAll/rootSQL/ORM unchanged.

queue_and_unknown_commit.normal_consumer: Actual Worker queue dispatch uses the strict message guard, acknowledges only successful guarded cleanup, retries failures with bounded backoff.
queue_and_unknown_commit.dlq_fix: OrderQueueDeadLetterService now admits the same exact Supplier two-field UUID guard beside Admin. Existing test covers both and rejects objectKey, keys, supplierId, invalid/cased/non-v4/missing UUID. No caller-selected object path is replayable.
queue_and_unknown_commit.pre_post_enqueue: Durable cleanup enqueue precedes every provider put/compose; failure prevents provider write. Successful provider write is followed by fresh cleanup enqueue to collect objects arriving after cancellation/expiry/deletion cleanup.
queue_and_unknown_commit.commit_uncertainty: No failure/unknown COMMIT authorizes deletion of final object. Recovery reads terminal SQL receipt and preserves the same attachment/final key.
queue_and_unknown_commit.guarded_cleanup: Consumer accepts only uploadId, re-reads strict SQL root under its guard, derives tenant+actor paths, defers active roots, and never trusts caller keys. Committed final key is eligible only after an all-owner actual attachment lookup under the real library fence finds no remaining reference.
queue_and_unknown_commit.known_extreme_residual: If post-write enqueue fails after an old pre-write message has already been consumed, an in-flight provider write can leave a residual object until an explicit later guarded cleanup/retry. The request reports unknown and does not delete the final object; this extreme boundary is not claimed solved by pre/post enqueue.
other_boundaries: Legacy MD5 cannot attest whole original bytes or authorize changed content.
No automatic cleanup of unregistered old Supplier protocol objects or historic public upload files.
Deletion/Queue/runtime/provider production behavior and operational rollout remain explicitly unexecuted.
